title: Adaptive allocation between weight-space and activation-space views
hypothesis: A per-function selector over weight-space and activation-space encodings lowers actual bytes versus either fixed allocation at the same preregistered output reconstruction tolerance.
physical_object: Pinned Pythia-70M-deduped output projection W with 512 input coordinates
mirror_coordinate: Per-function representation family and its serialized code
logical_multiplicity: Sixteen synthetic output-delta functions per world
controls: fixed activation coordinate solved through W
native shared output basis W plus private activation code

development.selection_metric: minimum actual serialized payload among methods with support relative RMSE <= 0.01

paid_objects: all NPZ arrays and metadata per function/world
common Pythia base checkpoint exactly once; its output basis W is already paid state

numerics: Read the pinned safetensors F16 output projection exactly and cast to F32/F64 for deterministic arithmetic; no checkpoint tensor is modified.
success_gate: On every fresh world, adaptive payload is at least 10% smaller than each fixed all-weight and all-activation payload, while heldout relative RMSE <= 0.01 and support relative RMSE <= 0.01.
failure_gate: Any fresh world misses quality, or adaptive fails to beat both fixed allocations by 10% actual NPZ bytes.
boundaries: Synthetic linear output-delta mechanism assay only
No natural LM quality or capacity claim
Native basis/low-rank coding may fully explain any result
No fresh result may affect protocol or thresholds
